title: Compute brief - 23 October 2026
description: Capital, not demand, is now the stated bottleneck: Jensen Huang says demand for capital exceeds supply, CoreWeave fell 10% on a Bernstein cut, and Sundar Pichai says everyone is short of compute into 2027. Kazakhstan licenses 45,000 Grace Blackwell GPUs, Amazon drops data centers on its Loudoun site, and China orders 3 million compliant NVIDIA cards. Tape: 69 confirms, 1 tick (Crusoe B300 $9.90 to $8.96), 0 NEW.
og_kicker: Everyone is short of compute, and the money to build it is getting scarcer
lede: The buyers and the builders agree there is not enough compute. The disagreement is over who pays for it. Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai said this week that everyone is short and that a customer asking Google for capacity in 2027 is incredibly difficult to serve. Jensen Huang told CNBC in Berlin that the demand for capital is much greater than the availability of capital, and put a 1 GW data center at about $50 billion. Markets are pricing that gap into the neoclouds: CoreWeave fell 10% on 22 October after Bernstein cut its target to $51 from $74, with Nebius down 7%, IREN 8% and Applied Digital 9%, and CoreWeave's unsecured bonds yield about 15%. Tesla went the other way and cut its 2026 capex outlook to about $20 billion from more than $25 billion. On the public tape, Crusoe cut its HGX B300 on-demand list to $8.96 from $9.90, down 9.5%, two days after its CEO said rental prices are rising. Everything else confirmed.

countries.name: Kazakhstan
countries.note: Firebird signs an investment agreement with the government and holds a US export license for 45,000 Grace Blackwell GPUs; phase one with Kazakhtelecom at Data Center Valley targets Q3 2027, about 500 MW potential with phase two (Wire, 23 Oct).

countries.name: United States
countries.note: Loudoun supervisors approve a preliminary deal under which Amazon drops data centers on its GW campus site, gives the county 25 acres worth about $65 million and $5 million for housing (Wire, 20 Oct). Pause on new data center applications deferred to 17 Nov.

countries.name: China
countries.note: Reuters: ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent order more than 3 million RTX PRO 5500 cards worth over $35 billion; NVIDIA may fill only 5% to 10% (Wire, 20 Oct; single source).

countries.name: Spain
countries.note: IREN secures grid power and the civil works license for a planned 300 MW AI campus in Badajoz, operations targeted for 2028 (Wire, 21 Oct).

silicon.name: B300 HGX
silicon.note: Tick: $9.90 on 22 Oct to $8.96 on 23 Oct (-9.5%). Crusoe re-laid its GPU table; B200 on-demand still Contact sales

watch.name: Alphabet, Microsoft (28 Oct) and Amazon (29 Oct)
watch.note: Pichai says Google is capacity constrained daily and 2027 capacity is hard to promise. Watch 2027 capex signals, lease commitments and third-party cloud spend after Meta raised its floor and Tesla cut.

watch.name: SK hynix (28 Oct), Samsung and Intel (29 Oct)
watch.note: HBM4 pricing and long-term agreements after record October chip exports; Intel's D-series inference GPU is sampling.

watch.name: Neocloud credit and CoreWeave Q3
watch.note: CoreWeave down 29% in October through 21 Oct, unsecured bonds near 15%; credit desks told CNBC high-yield issuance is on hold until after the 3 Nov midterms. CoreWeave reports in November.

watch.name: Loudoun data center pause vote
watch.note: Resolution to pause data center and substation legislative applications for up to 12 months deferred to the 17 Nov board meeting; Amazon GW campus terms still to be finalised.

watch.name: China RTX PRO 5500 allocations
watch.note: Samples due December, deliveries from Q1 2027. Watch whether NVIDIA confirms allocations or US licensing changes.
